title: spectral-ingress-shaper-and-tenant-aware-mini-batcher-to-reduce-embedding-tail-latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: decrease tail latency (p95/p99) for the embeddings endpoint under mixed-tenant traffic without regressing median latency or increasing token cost. Success criteria: p99 decrease by >=25% on production-like load, no >5% regression in p50, and stable CPU/GPU utilization across tenants. Approach: 1) Spectral latency decomposition to classify tail causes (ingress spikes, stragglers, kernel hot paths). 2) Implement an ingress shaper that enforces soft deadlines per-tenant and assigns request hedging/priority buckets. 3) Tenant-aware mini-batcher that picks per-tenant batch size targets using queue depth, recent service-time distribution, and sequence-length percentiles; integrates kernel-hint metadata to prefer low-latency kernels for short sequences and quantized kernels for large batched loads. 4) Kernel hinting API: propagate sequence-length histogram and deadline window to the runtime so kernel selector can prefer fused or cuBLAS paths. 5) Fallback hedging policy: opportunistic speculative duplicate to fast-path queue when a request crosses a latency threshold. Deliverables: prototype ingress-shaper, mini-batcher algorithm, kernel-hint propagation, evaluation reports and perf dashboard filters per-tenant.
steps: Added lightweight ingress sampler to collect per-tenant arrival curve and sequence-length histogram (done)
Implemented spectral profiler to label tail events by cause (in PR)
Build tenant-aware mini-batcher with soft-deadline scheduling and dynamic target batch size (in progress)
Expose kernel-hint metadata in request envelope and adapt runtime selector (blocked by runtime integration)
Run canary against staging with mixed-tenancy replay workload and collect p50/p95/p99 and cost metrics (pending)
observations: Initial spectral profiling of 48h production sample: 62% of p99 events align with short, high-priority bursts causing queue saturation; 28% correlate with long sequences that trigger slow kernels; 10% unexplained async stragglers.
Microbenchmarks with local mini-batcher prototype: under synthetic burstwork p99 reduced ~18% but p50 increased 3% due to extra scheduling latency for tiny requests.

Kernel hint experiments on dev: selecting fused-attn kernel for seq<=128 reduced per-token latency by ~9% compared to default selector for small batches; fallbacks to quantized kernel saved GPU cycles for large batches with small accuracy delta (<0.5% embed cosine change on eval set).
risks_and_tradeoffs: Additional orchestration in ingress path increases median latency slightly for smallest requests; mitigated by fast-path bypass for tiny low-cost requests.
Kernel hints expose heuristics that might need frequent tuning across model families — we will gate heuristics behind a per-model config and metric-driven rollouts.
Speculative hedging increases GPU utilization and potential cost; limit to high-latency-critical tenants or when SLA risk detected.
metrics: Baseline staging (mixed replay): p50=12ms, p95=42ms, p99=128ms
Prototype mini-batcher (burst workload): p50=13ms (+1ms), p95=36ms (-6ms), p99=105ms (-18ms)
Target: p99<=96ms across 95% of tenants under policy constraints
